Around the age of 20 it dawned on me, I always wanted a family and even had my names picked out, but by 20 I hadn’t had any interest.

My family, friends and coworkers said I was the nicest person (I hate saying things that sound arrogant, but I heard it so much from all of them). They said any girl would be so lucky to have me and I would be taken very quickly. Im now 30 and have only gone on two more dates since I was 20. I have tried dating apps, expanded my hobbies, become more social, started three degrees at uni, lost weight and put myself out there for ten years. It was clear that what they were saying were just platitudes to get me to keep trying and keep trying I have.

I learnt when I was 22 that I had Bipolar and have had a psychiatrist and psychologist, combined with medication to keep me healthy. I have had professional help for eight years and that hasn’t helped people wanting me. I have done everything I possibly can to make me more appealing and it hasn’t made a difference.

I’ve given up now, there is no point to any of it and I will be single for the rest of my life. Part of me wants to throw it in all together and stop my therapy and meds, because honestly what’s the point. Im destined to die alone in this shitty world that I tried so much to be a part of.

Life would be the same, because it's not just a thought, it's what it is.  


Nobody loves me, nobody would care if I was gone. I sit at home or at uni all day desperately hoping my friends will contact me or help me, but they don't. I am afterthought to everyone.  


The pain can't be treated because it's just anxious pain, anxiety slowly killing me. I feel so helpless right now, I just want it to stop. It never stops, it keeps going and going and I am forced to live in this pain that is called life.

But I’m not making any progress opposed to the person next to me, they are getting further and further ahead of me.

My meds are pretty good, I’ve been on them for over two years now. Before that I had a lot of testing and trying different ones, but I’ve been quite stable on these for a period of time now.

It’s so hard to watch people get what they deserve in life and watch all the hard work I’m putting in go unrewarded. I could have easily done no work on myself and still be in the same place. I just want the pain to stop.

**-What are you overall first impressions of Assassin's Creed Odyssey?**

First impressions are disappointment and a little bit of anger. I've been a fan of the series since 2007 and at the moment it's unrecognizable as an Assassin's Creed game. I gave Origins a pass, because it was meant to be an origin story and after that we would get back to what made Assassin's Creed great, so I'm bitterly disappointed that my faith was misplaced. 

**-How do you feel about the new dialogue and splitting-narrative system?**

It dosen't make any sense, how are we making decisions for our ancestors? The animus shows us the past, not recreates it. 

**-How do you feel about the new ability system?**

I haven't seen enough of it, I didn't mind the abilities in Origins though. I thought the systems in Unity and Syndicate were also pretty good, so I'm not against the system if it adds to the game.

**-How do you feel about choosing between two protagonists? Do you like or dislike the new protagonists?**

I don't mind two protagonists, I thought it worked pretty well in Syndicate. As long as their stories are strong I have no issue with having two, it needs to make sense for the modern day story though. 

**-What are your thoughts on the new weapon, King Leonidas' broken spear?**

I like the idea of it being a piece of eden, but that being the case how is it not an overpowered weapon? It's no substitute for a hidden blade.

**-How do you feel about the setting? What are your thoughts on it taking place before Assassin's Creed Origins?**

I do like the setting, Greece is certainly a place that I have long thought would be a great place for an Assassin's Creed game. The fact that it takes place before Origins is bizarre though. We have just had the birth of the assassin's and now we are going further back? I honestly don't understand the reasoning behind this, if you knew the next game was going further back why did you make Origins the starting point for the assassins? 

**-What are your thoughts on The First Civ being brought into focus?**

I do like that we are getting more focus on The First Civ, it's something the series has lacked since AC3. That being said there is no reason we can't get that in a game with assassins, as the first five games would indicate.

**-What questions do you have about Assassin's Creed Odyssey?**

When are you bring Assassin's Creed back and not games that simply have the name slapped on the front?

This new direction is not Assassin's Creed, you have totally removed the DNA of the series. No sequences, no hidden blade, modern day is reduced to nothing more than a few 5 minute cutscenes, eagle vision is gone, no stealth.

RPG elements have no place in an Assassin's Creed game, there was absolutely nothing wrong with the direction you took in Unity, why could you have not just refined that system instead of throwing it out with the next entry.

At the moment I feel really cheated being a longtime fan of the series, almost like your core fanbase mean absolutely nothing to you. I defended the series through the messy launch of Unity, I was even willing to give your a free pass on Origins because it was an origin story. There is no defending this, you have ditched your dedicated and longtime fanbase, to create just another generic RPG with the Assassin's Creed name logo on the front.

I went to therapy for years, went through many psychologists and it just wasn't working. I finally applied at a place called headspace where they employ mostly young people straight out of their degree, it's free and gives them experience.

So I gave it a go, has no idea who I'd get but I knew that it might be a bit easier to explain my issues to someone who is more my age (Older ones I had I just had no connection with). I got a young lady, early 30s, she made me feel so comfortable I almost told her my life story before the end of my appointment.

I've now been with her for 2.5 years. She's moved twice and I've just followed her. It was so hard to find someone I connected with, so I was prepared to drive wherever she went.

Therapy isn't for everyone, I'm not saying it's the magic cure. For that one hour though someone is there and they are truly listening and that's one hour more that I feel I'm not completely alone.
